What does code generation mean in software development?
Code generation is the practice of producing new source code, either written by a developer or created automatically by tools, to implement features or structures in an application.

What is boilerplate code?
Boilerplate code is repetitive, standard code that must be included in many places with little or no change, such as setup, configuration, or class definitions.

What is scaffolding in app development?
Scaffolding is the automatic generation of a basic project or component structure, giving developers a working starting point they can build upon.

What is clean code?
Clean code is code that is easy to read, understand, and maintain, with clear naming, small functions, and minimal complexity.

Why is readability important when generating code?
Readable code is easier for others (and your future self) to understand, debug, and extend, which reduces errors and lowers long-term maintenance cost.

What are naming conventions and why do they matter?
Naming conventions are agreed rules for naming variables, functions, and classes; they make code consistent, predictable, and easier to read across a team.

What makes a good function name?
A good function name clearly describes what the function does, is concise, uses consistent style, and avoids ambiguous or misleading terms.

Why should functions do only one thing?
A function that does one thing is easier to understand, test, reuse, and change, and it reduces the chance of unintended side effects.

What is the difference between a comment and self-documenting code?
A comment is explanatory text added to code, while self-documenting code uses clear naming and structure so the code explains itself with little need for comments.

When should you write comments?
Comments are most useful for explaining why something is done, clarifying complex logic, or documenting decisions, rather than restating what the code obviously does.

What is a pure function?
A pure function always returns the same output for the same input and has no side effects, making it predictable and easy to test.

What is a side effect in programming?
A side effect is any change a function makes outside its own scope, such as modifying a global variable, writing to a file, or updating a database.

What is the importance of consistent code formatting?
Consistent formatting makes code easier to read and review, reduces noise in version control, and is often enforced automatically with linters and formatters.

What is a code style guide?
A code style guide is a set of conventions for writing code in a consistent way across a project or team, covering formatting, naming, and structure.

What is refactoring?
Refactoring is the process of restructuring existing code to improve its readability, structure, and maintainability without changing its external behavior.

Why is refactoring important?
Refactoring keeps a codebase healthy by reducing complexity and duplication, making it easier to add features, fix bugs, and onboard new developers.

What is a code smell?
A code smell is a sign in the code that may indicate a deeper problem, such as duplicated logic, overly long functions, or tangled dependencies.

What are some common code smells?
Common code smells include duplicated code, long methods, large classes, long parameter lists, magic numbers, and deeply nested conditionals.

What is the DRY principle?
DRY stands for 'Don't Repeat Yourself', a principle that encourages eliminating duplication by extracting shared logic into a single reusable place.

What is the difference between refactoring and rewriting?
Refactoring improves existing code incrementally while preserving behavior, whereas rewriting replaces code with a new implementation from scratch.

What is the 'Extract Method' refactoring?
Extract Method takes a block of code and moves it into its own well-named function, improving readability and enabling reuse.

What is the 'Rename Variable' refactoring?
Renaming a variable replaces an unclear or misleading name with a clearer one, making the code's intent easier to understand.

What are magic numbers and why are they a problem?
Magic numbers are unexplained literal values in code; they reduce readability and should be replaced with named constants that explain their meaning.

Why are long methods considered a problem?
Long methods are harder to read, test, and reuse, and they often combine multiple responsibilities that should be split into smaller functions.

What is a large class code smell?
A large class tries to do too much, holding too many responsibilities; it should usually be split into smaller, more focused classes.

How can tests help when refactoring?
Tests verify that behavior stays the same before and after refactoring, giving confidence that changes did not introduce bugs.

When is the best time to refactor code?
Good times to refactor include before adding a feature to messy code, after getting tests passing, or whenever a code smell makes a change harder than it should be.

What is technical debt?
Technical debt is the implied future cost of choosing a quick or easy solution now instead of a better approach that would take longer.

How does refactoring relate to technical debt?
Refactoring is one of the main ways to pay down technical debt by gradually improving code that was written hastily or has become outdated.

What is the 'Replace Conditional with Polymorphism' refactoring?
It replaces complex conditional logic that varies by type with polymorphic objects, so each type handles its own behavior, simplifying the code.

What is the Boy Scout Rule in coding?
The Boy Scout Rule says to always leave the code a little cleaner than you found it, encouraging small, continuous improvements.

What are the SOLID principles?
SOLID is a set of five design principles for writing maintainable object-oriented code: Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, and Dependency Inversion.

What is the Single Responsibility Principle?
The Single Responsibility Principle states that a class or module should have only one reason to change, meaning it should do one well-defined job.

What is the Open/Closed Principle?
The Open/Closed Principle states that software entities should be open for extension but closed for modification, so behavior can be added without changing existing code.

What is the Liskov Substitution Principle?
The Liskov Substitution Principle states that objects of a subclass should be usable in place of objects of the parent class without breaking the program.

What is the Interface Segregation Principle?
The Interface Segregation Principle states that clients should not be forced to depend on interfaces they do not use, favoring small, specific interfaces.

What is the Dependency Inversion Principle?
The Dependency Inversion Principle states that high-level modules should depend on abstractions rather than on concrete low-level implementations.

What is the KISS principle?
KISS stands for 'Keep It Simple, Stupid', a principle that favors simple, straightforward solutions over unnecessary complexity.

What is the YAGNI principle?
YAGNI stands for 'You Aren't Gonna Need It', a principle that advises against building functionality until it is actually needed.

What is modular code?
Modular code is organized into independent, self-contained units that each handle a specific responsibility, making the system easier to develop and maintain.

What is code reusability?
Code reusability is the practice of writing code that can be used in multiple places or projects, reducing duplication and development effort.

Why is consistent error handling a good practice?
Consistent error handling makes failures predictable and easier to debug, and it prevents unexpected crashes or silent failures across the codebase.
